The presenter, Sarah Khalifa, 39, is best known for her programme Mission Impossible, which dealt with issues concerning security and crime.

The petition will be lodged with Charles, Jamaica’s head of state, on Monday.

guardian.description:
Beijing wants banks and insurers to bolster investment in stock market as it helps to replenish cash reserves

China will inject $54bn (£40bn) into its financial sector as Beijing attempts to shore up banks and insurers in the face of faltering economic growth.

A host of financial institutions said they were due to receive billions of yuan in capital from state institutions including the ministry of finance and even the company that runs the country’s tobacco monopoly.

rfi.title: Internal inquiry opened after Eiffel Tower 'sexist' closure prompts strike
rfi.description: The Eiffel Tower reopened on Tuesday after staff walked out over the removal of women colleagues during a visit by a Hindu religious group which later apologised. The operating company has acknowledged it was wrong to accept the conditions and has opened an internal investigation.

rfi.title: Hunt on for thieves after Renoir museum raid in southern France
rfi.description: A search is under way for the thieves who stole several paintings from a museum dedicated to the French Impressionist painter Pierre-Auguste Renoir in the south of France in the early hours of Tuesday morning.

rfi.title: French firefighters begin six-week strike over funding after record summer fires
rfi.description: French professional firefighters launch a six-week nationwide campaign on Tuesday, demanding more funding, staff and better protection for their health after a summer of unprecedented wildfires.

rfi.title: France tries 14 over deadliest Channel migrant crossing disaster
rfi.description: Fourteen people are to go on trial in France on Tuesday over the loss of 31 people including a seven-year-old child in 2021, in the deadliest small-boat crossing accident recorded in the Channel.

rfi.title: Merz ‘deeply shocked’ as far-right victory tests Germany’s political firewall
rfi.description: The fallout from the AfD’s landslide in Saxony-Anhalt is testing Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s reform agenda, Germany’s support for Ukraine and the political firewall designed to keep the far-right out of power.

rfi.title: EU chief unveils €200m Greenland package amid tensions over Trump claims
rfi.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen unveiled a 200-million-euro investment package for Greenland during the second of a two-day visit. The European Union has increased its focus on the vast, strategic island since President Donald Trump began insisting that the United States should take control of it for security reasons.

rfi.title: Sons of Yemen ex-president on trial in France over alleged stolen assets
rfi.description: Two sons of former Yemeni president Ali Abdullah Saleh are on trial in Paris on Monday, accused of embezzling public funds that were used to buy luxury property worth €16 million in Paris.

rfi.title: Jamaica steps up slavery reparations campaign with petition to King Charles III
rfi.description: Jamaica is testing a new legal route in its long-running campaign for slavery reparations, asking Britain’s monarch to put key questions before the Privy Council.

rfi.title: France, South Korea announce billion-euro investment for audiovisual industry
rfi.description: France and South Korea will invest one billion euros to support the audiovisual and entertainment sector, President Emmanuel Macron said as he brought together some of the world's top entertainment bosses for a summit on the future of cinema.

rfi.title: Far-right activists stand trial in Paris over killing of rugby star Aramburu
rfi.description: Two far-right activists go on trial in Paris on Monday over the 2022 killing of former Argentina rugby international Federico Martin Aramburu, who was shot dead following a late-night altercation in the French capital.

rfi.title: Global film industry gathers in France to tackle 'unprecedented challenges'
rfi.description: Some 200 cinema and entertainment professionals from around the world are gathering in the south of France on Monday to discuss the future of creative sectors threatened by artificial intelligence, streaming and competition from online platforms.

rfi.title: Visa Pour l'Image: Tato wins top prize for Madagascar protest coverage
rfi.description: AFP photographer Luis Tato on Saturday won the top award at the prestigious Visa Pour l'Image photojournalism festival in Perpignan, southern France.

rfi.title: US envoys Witkoff and Kushner arrive in Kyiv after talks with Putin in Russia
rfi.description: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Kyiv on Sunday for talks with the Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky a day after meeting the Russian president Vladimir Putin to discuss proposals over how to end the four-year war between Russia and Ukraine.

rfi.title: France's school uniform experiment unravels with only mixed results
rfi.description: Two years after France began trialling uniforms in schools, the experiment is sputtering to a close after failing to convince pupils or teachers.

rfi.title: Driven from their island, Zambian fishermen pay price of Chinese expansion
rfi.description: Hundreds of fishermen say they were violently driven from an island in southern Zambia and have been unable to return to their fishing grounds for more than three years, after a Chinese-owned fishing company expanded its operations in the area. They say they lost their homes and livelihoods, have never received compensation and are still seeking justice. An RFI investigation has traced what happened to the community and the Chinese company's growing presence on Lake Kariba.

rfi.title: Turkey seeks Black Sea shipping deal as attacks threaten grain trade
rfi.description: Turkey is racing to restore safe passage for cargo ships in the Black Sea as attacks on shipping disrupt grain exports and push up prices. Russia and Ukraine are major global wheat exporters, but Black Sea trade has been severely disrupted as both sides step up attacks on shipping and port infrastructure.

rfi.title: UN backs effort to drop Mercator map and show size of Africa more accurately
rfi.description: The United Nations voted on Saturday for a shift away from the 16th-century Mercator global map towards one more accurately reflecting the true size of countries.

rfi.title: French tennis player Gea hails surge into second week at US Open
rfi.description: Unseeded Frenchman Arthur Gea declared himself physcially fit and ready to fight on Monday night for a first appearance in the quarter-finals at a Grand Slam tournament.

euronews.title: Sweden heads to polls in close election race dominated by welfare state and security
euronews.description: Opinion polls ahead of Sunday's vote point to a victory for the centre-left opposition headed by the Social Democrats which could see Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson's centre-right coalition ousted.

euronews.title: Fancy a trip to Canada? These airlines are launching new routes from Europe
euronews.description: Seasonal routes are opening up destinations like Toronto, Montréal and Halifax for more Europeans.

euronews.title: Brussels Airport reconnects to Europe’s high-speed rail network after more than 10 years
euronews.description: Belgium’s largest airport is back on Europe’s high-speed rail map after more than a decade, with a new Deutsche Bahn service connecting Brussels Airport with Cologne and Antwerp.

euronews.title: Turkey's Kılıçdaroğlu opens door to İmamoğlu presidential bid in Euronews interview
euronews.description: In an exclusive interview with Euronews, Kılıçdaroğlu defended his court-ordered return to the CHP leadership, said İmamoğlu is not a political prisoner but should not have been detained, and left the door open to backing İmamoğlu in a presidential bid.

euronews.title: Six months into Hormuz blockade, Qatar and UAE test ways to keep LNG moving
euronews.description: LNG exporters are looking for ways around the disruption in Hormuz, with three Gulf cargoes recently moved using ship-to-ship transfers (STS) as Qatar and UAE exports remain far below pre-war levels.

euronews.title: EU countries discuss ‘realistic acceptable volume’ for Europe-wide taxes
euronews.description: The Irish presidency wants EU member states to set a realistic revenue target for new Europe-wide taxes as it prepares a new compromise proposal on how to fund the next budget.

euronews.title: Pupils' reading and maths skills slump across the world as digitalisation soars, PISA study shows
euronews.description: Student performance in reading, maths and science is declining across OECD countries, and the traditional divide between advantaged students and disadvantaged pupils no longer holds. How do EU countries measure up?

euronews.title: German exports fall for first time in five months, deepening recovery fears
euronews.description: Germany's export engine is sputtering. Shipments fell in July for the first time in five months, as weaker demand from China and the eurozone outweighed a rebound in US trade.

euronews.title: Spanish archaeologists find 4,400-year-old tomb in Egypt with original colours intact
euronews.description: A Spanish-Egyptian archaeological team has unearthed at Saqqara an exceptional late Fifth Dynasty tomb with two funerary chapels and reliefs of farming scenes and offering processions that still retain their original colours.

euronews.title: Sweden to buy Lockheed Martin's HIMARS rocket artillery in €630 million deal
euronews.description: Sweden's government has authorised its armed forces to buy the US-made HIMARS rocket artillery system from Lockheed Martin for around 7 billion Swedish crowns, almost €630 million, and has signed a parallel agreement with Finland to operate the two countries' rocket artillery together.

euronews.title: Iconic Evil Dead star Bruce Campbell says he has five years to live after cancer diagnosis
euronews.description: The actor first disclosed his diagnosis in March, saying that he had a "treatable" but not "curable" form of cancer.

euronews.title: Ukraine's prosecutor general resigns amid major corruption investigation
euronews.description: Ruslan Kravchenko stepped down after investigators uncovered an alleged criminal organisation, whose members allegedly received bribes from fraudulent call centres and laundered millions.

euronews.title: Jaguar Land Rover cuts 4,000 jobs worldwide in effort to save costs
euronews.description: JLR said it would cut around 4,000 roles worldwide over the next two years as part of its plan to simplify its organisation and generate £1.7 billion (€2bn) in savings.

euronews.title: Russia and North Korea open first road bridge across border
euronews.description: Russia and North Korea have opened their first road bridge across their shared border, linking the two countries over the Tumen River.

euronews.title: UK commits €116m for Ukraine's winter air defence, including Patriot missiles
euronews.description: Britain has been one of Ukraine's biggest backers in its effort to repel Russia following Moscow's full-scale invasion of its neighbour in February 2022.

euronews.title: The European commute: Which EU country spends the most time getting to work?
euronews.description: Just how long do Europeans spend getting to work? Across the continent, the daily average commute sits at 48 minutes, but that hides a massive divide.

euronews.title: Argentina sues Israeli oil firm as Ben Gvir urges Netanyahu to back its Falklands claim
euronews.description: Argentina is to file criminal charges against several companies linked to Israeli oil firm Navitas for operating without authorisation in the Falklands, as Milei steps up his offensive against the Sea Lion project with new sanctions and measures to bolster territorial defence.

euronews.title: Robot revolt? Polish company stages protest demanding stricter AI rules
euronews.description: In Warsaw, marching robots waved flags and chanted slogans outside the digital affairs ministry, calling on Poland's government to regulate AI before it costs people their jobs.

lemonde.title: PISA 2025 : pour Edouard Geffray, ministre de l’éducation, « on aurait dû s’interroger plus tôt sur les mesures à prendre pour le collège »
lemonde.description: Alors que les résultats montrent que les élèves français décrochent, selon l’enquête de l’OCDE publiée mardi, le ministre de l’éducation fait le constat d’« un phénomène de fond », celui d’un changement dans la manière dont on éduque les enfants, très exposés aux réseaux sociaux. Il propose de clarifier auprès des familles les objectifs d’apprentissage.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : après une nouvelle attaque russe, Volodymyr Zelensky veut demander à Donald Trump des missiles pour protéger son pays
lemonde.description: Le président ukrainien a déclaré que l’Ukraine avait besoin de missiles américains pour se protéger contre les attaques de missiles balistiques russes et qu’il comptait aborder cette question avec le président américain lors d’une rencontre prévue pour la seconde moitié de septembre.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : l’hypothèse d’une primaire agite encore la droite et le bloc central
lemonde.description: Face à la perspective d’être absentes au second tour du scrutin présidentiel, plusieurs figures macronistes ou des Républicains plaident pour un mode de départage organisé. Si Edouard Philippe refuse d’en entendre parler, Gabriel Attal et Bruno Retailleau laissent l’idée prospérer.

lemonde.title: L’Iran brandit la menace d’une escalade militaire pour briser le blocus américain
lemonde.description: Téhéran, dont les exportations de brut sont réduites à peu de chose, peine à trouver des ressources budgétaires. Le régime iranien pourrait être tenté de mettre à profit la perspective des élections américaines de mi-mandat pour augmenter la pression militaire sur l’administration Trump.

lemonde.title: 7-Octobre : Benyamin Nétanyahou mis en cause après la publication d’une enquête journalistique affirmant qu’il a été informé d’une attaque à venir
lemonde.description: Selon « Haaretz », qui reprend les informations d’un livre à paraître, le chef du Hamas a informé un intermédiaire qu’« une opération terrifiante » était en préparation. L’information serait remontée jusqu’au président des Emirats arabes unis, qui l’a transmise au premier ministre israélien. M. Nétanyahou dénonce un « mensonge total ».

lemonde.title: Le Musée Renoir de Cagnes-sur-mer cambriolé, deux tableaux sur les quatre volés ont été récupérés
lemonde.description: Deux voleurs se sont introduits mardi 8 septembre dans le musée situé dans la ville des Alpes-Maritimes. Ils ont dérobé quatre œuvres, mais deux ont été abandonnées dans leur fuite, a fait savoir le maire, Bryan Masson.

lemonde.title: Emmanuel Macron demande à Ursula von der Leyen une interdiction européenne des réseaux sociaux aux moins de 15 ans
lemonde.description: La présidente de la Commission européenne, qui a promis des propositions après l’été, a dit envisager un accès progressif et gradué pour différentes classes d’âge. Elle abordera le sujet à l’occasion de son discours sur l’état de l’Union, le 16 septembre.

lemonde.title: Le patron d’Audi appelle l’Europe à durcir le ton face aux constructeurs automobiles chinois
lemonde.description: Le PDG du constructeur allemand, Gernot Döllner, demande à la Commission européenne de renforcer ses mesures protectionnistes pour éviter de nouvelles suppressions d’emplois après la vague massive annoncée par sa maison mère Volkswagen.

lemonde.title: A Belgrade, des milliers de partisans de la « Grande Serbie » ont participé aux obsèques de Ratko Mladic
lemonde.description: L’ancien commandant de l’armée serbe en Bosnie-Herzégovine, condamné par la justice internationale pour génocide, crimes contre l’humanité et crimes de guerre lors des conflits dans l’ex-Yougoslavie dans les années 1990, et mort dans la prison de La Haye, a été enterré lundi dans la capitale serbe.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Raphaël Glucksmann rejette l’idée d’une primaire élargie à François Ruffin, estimant qu’« on ne change pas les règles en cours de jeu »
lemonde.description: L’ancien « insoumis » avait proposé au candidat de Place publique un débat sur sa possible participation à la primaire qui se tiendra les 9-10 et 16-17 octobre, ainsi que sur un possible abaissement du prix à 2 euros, au lieu des 15 actuellement prévus.

lemonde.title: Pourquoi les employeurs ne doivent pas attendre pour identifier et réguler les systèmes d’IA « à haut risque »
lemonde.description: Les services des ressources humaines doivent, d’ici à la fin 2027, recenser et clarifier les systèmes d’intelligence artificielle utilisés par leurs services, et informer les salariés, conseille le juriste Jean-Emmanuel Ray, qui revient dans sa chronique sur la partie concernant le travail de l’« AI Act ».

lemonde.title: Arthur Gea, dernier Français engagé à l’US Open, éliminé en huitièmes de finale
lemonde.description: Le tennisman de 21 ans, qui avait été repêché dans le tableau principal grâce à un forfait, a été renversé par le Néerlandais Botic van de Zandschulp au bout d’un match étouffant de cinq sets et plus de cinq heures.

lemonde.title: Flottille pour Gaza : nouvelle plainte contre Israël de 26 Français pour actes de torture
lemonde.description: Les plaignants dénoncent le détournement de leurs navires et leur arrestation arbitraire par les forces israéliennes, ainsi que des violences, telles que passage à tabac et coups de Taser, et des traitements inhumains ou dégradants.

lemonde.title: « La prochaine étape antigreenwashing ne pourra faire l’économie d’une réflexion sur les décideurs »
lemonde.description: La chercheuse en sciences de gestion Ouiam Kaddouri constate, dans une tribune au « Monde », que les nouvelles règles de l’Union européenne visant à donner plus d’autonomie aux consommateurs dans le cadre de la transition écologique ne s’adressent pas à ceux qui prennent vraiment les décisions.

lemonde.title: Les pompiers appelés à une mobilisation nationale pour réclamer plus de moyens, après un été marqué par des incendies d’une virulence inédite
lemonde.description: Le mouvement, prévu pour durer six semaines à compter de mardi, n’aura pas d’impact sur les secours car des réquisitions sont possibles. Mais les attentes sont très fortes et les pompiers professionnels comptent déployer banderoles et messages sur les camions.

zeit.description: Nach Sabotageakten in mehreren Bundesländern hat die Polizei den zuvor gesuchten Tatverdächtigen gefasst. Zur Festnahme kam es in der Nähe des Kraftwerks Weisweiler.

zeit.title: Unfälle: Sieben Kinder bei Unfall zwischen Bus und Lastwagen verletzt
Staatsschutz ermittelt: 17-Jähriger angegriffen und homophob beleidigt
Ekelerregender Vorfall: Vier Männer urinieren am Bahnhof auf Fußgängerrampe
Entscheidung am 26. September: Kampf um Olympia: München hofft auf «Spiele des Herzens»
Bildungstest: Nach Pisa-Ergebnissen: Jung denkt über weitere Reformen nach
Verdacht des Rechtsextremismus: Wüst will verfassungsrechtliche Prüfung der AfD
zeit.description: Hendrik Wüst fordert eine neue Arbeitsgruppe von Bund und Ländern. Diese soll überprüfen, wie die AfD zum Grundgesetz steht. Um ein Verbot gehe es nicht unbedingt.

zeit.title: DFB-Pokal: Ermittlungen gegen Polizisten nach Einsatz bei Pokalderby
zeit.description: Beim Pokalspiel zwischen Mannheim und Kaiserslautern kam es zu Ausschreitungen. Ermittelt wird unter anderem gegen einen Polizisten, der an dem Abend im Einsatz war.

zeit.title: Wahl in Sachsen-Anhalt: AfD lädt alle Parteien in Sachsen-Anhalt zu Sondierungsgesprächen ein
zeit.description: Die AfD lädt in Sachsen-Anhalt alle im Landtag vertretenen Parteien zu Gesprächen ein. BSW-Spitzenkandidatin Claudia Wittig erteilt der AfD im Voraus eine Absage.

zeit.title: Ungarn und Russland: Ungarn weist zehn russische Diplomaten aus
zeit.description: Ungarn hat zehn Mitglieder der russischen Vertretung aufgefordert, das Land zu verlassen. Das russische Außenministerium droht mit einer »harten Reaktion«.

zeit.title: Krieg gegen die Ukraine: Selenskyj erwartet baldiges Treffen mit Trump
zeit.description: Der ukrainische Präsident lobt »anständige Ideen« der US-Verhandler für ein Kriegsende. Russland attackiert Kyjiw nach dem Ende einer Feuerpause. Das Liveblog

zeit.title: Zitronen-Basilikum-Posset: Britischer geht Dessert gar nicht
zeit.description: Schon Shakespeare ließ seine Helden Possets verschlingen, manchmal war das Dessert vergiftet. Diese Version ist harmlos, fix gemacht – und die Sahne herrlich geschmeidig.

nzz.title: INTERAKTIV - Union fällt in neuer Umfrage unter 20 Prozent – alle Umfragen zur Bundestagswahl
nzz.description: Wie würden die Deutschen wählen, wenn am Sonntag Bundestagswahl wäre? Die neuesten Umfragen im NZZ-Wahltrend – täglich aktualisiert.

nzz.title: Novartis erleidet einen weiteren Rückschlag in der Forschung – der Aktienkurs bricht um über 10 Prozent ein
nzz.description: Ein neuer Wirkstoff von Novartis gegen eine bisher unbehandelbare Muskelerkrankung hat sich in der späten klinischen Entwicklung als Flop erwiesen. Dies wirft die Frage auf, ob der Pharmakonzern für seine bis anhin teuerste Firmenübernahme zu viel bezahlt hat.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Polizei-News aus Zürich: Mann am Bahnhof Richtung einfahrenden Zug gestossen
nzz.description: Die neusten Polizeimeldungen aus der Region.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Lage im Gazastreifen: Israelische Luftwaffe setzt Angriffe im Gazastreifen fort
nzz.description: Die Waffenruhe zwischen Israel und der Hamas ist instabil, die humanitäre Not im Gazastreifen ist gross. Der Friedensplan der USA wurde bisher nur teilweise umgesetzt. Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Wirtschaft: Ehemaliger Schweizer Top-Banker wegen Korruption vor Gericht +++ Deutsche Exporte sind rückläufig
INTERAKTIV - Die Stromtarife sinken, aber nicht überall – in welchen Gemeinden die Preise 2027 besonders günstig sind
nzz.description: Die Haushalte können beim Strom im Schnitt 53 Franken sparen. Die regionalen Unterschiede bleiben jedoch gross. Besonders in der Ostschweiz müssen sich viele Kunden auf höhere Tarife einstellen.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Kultur: Diebe stehlen drei Gemälde aus französischem Renoir-Museum
DATENANALYSE - Die AfD triumphiert in Sachsen-Anhalt – und beweist, dass alle anderen sie völlig falsch eingeschätzt haben
nzz.description: Jahrelang redeten Politbeobachter die AfD als Protestpartei klein, die von den Verlierern der Globalisierung gewählt werde. Eine genauere Betrachtung der Wahldaten zeigt: Die Partei ist über einfache sozioökonomische Erklärungsansätze hinausgewachsen.

nzz.title: Pisa-Bilanz der Schweiz: Stark, aber nicht stark genug
nzz.description: In der neuen Pisa-Bildungsstudie schneiden Schülerinnen und Schüler in der Schweiz international gesehen gut ab. Aber: Sie werden – wie Jugendliche überall auf der Welt – immer schlechter im Lesen und Rechnen.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Mehr als 70 Verletzte bei Huthi-Angriffen in Saudiarabien +++ Elf Tote bei weiteren Angriffen Israels in Libanon
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: Der Gipfel der «Peinlichkeit»: In Österreich verliert ein falscher Dreitausender seinen Namen
nzz.description: Ein Grat am Grossvenediger wurde vor 38 Jahren künstlich auf 3000 Meter erhöht und nach dem Gletscherforscher Wolfgang Pillewizer benannt: einem überzeugten Nazi. Nun entzieht ihm der Österreichische Alpenverein die Ehrung.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Trumps zweite Amtszeit: Trump will den Verkauf der kanadischen Bombardier in den USA untersagen
nzz.description: Donald Trump regiert zum zweiten Mal als amerikanischer Präsident – mit weitreichenden innen- und aussenpolitischen Folgen. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Deutschland kann nicht jede Attacke verhindern – aber es sollte endlich vorbereitet sein
nzz.description: Der Hackerangriff auf Berlin zeigt exemplarisch, wie gross die Lücke zwischen politischen Erkenntnissen und tatsächlicher Widerstandsfähigkeit des Staates ist.

nzz.title: «Wir stehen wieder bei null»: Der Wiederaufbau nach der Sturzflut in Nepal wird Milliarden kosten
nzz.description: Das Himalaja-Land hatte sich noch nicht ganz von dem verheerenden Erdbeben von 2015 erholt, als es von der Flutwelle getroffen wurde. Der Wiederaufbau ist eine solch gewaltige Aufgabe, dass viele Überlebende nicht wissen, wo sie anfangen sollen.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Die Mega-Börsengänge von SpaceX, Anthropic und Co. schüren Furcht vor einer KI-Blase – doch Angst ist an der Börse ein schlechter Ratgeber
nzz.description: Der Boom der künstlichen Intelligenz (KI) treibt die Börsen seit Jahren an. Bei den angekündigten Riesenbörsengängen von KI-Unternehmen gibt es Warnzeichen. Langfristig orientierte Anleger sollten sich deshalb aber nicht verrückt machen.

france24fr.title: Egypte : la présentatrice de télévision Sarah Khalifa condamnée à mort
france24fr.description: D'après le journal Al-Ahram, le tribunal pénal du Caire "a condamné la productrice Sarah Khalifa et 11 autres accusés à la peine de mort par pendaison, pour "organisation criminelle spécialisée dans l'importation de substances utilisées dans la fabrication de drogues, en vue de les vendre". Sarah Khalifa, notamment connue pour son émission "mission difficile", consacrée aux sujets de sécurité et de criminalité, avait aussi été condamnée pour séquestration et agression d'un jeune homme.

france24fr.title: Volkswagen : à Osnabrück, les cabriolets vont céder la place à la défense aérienne
france24fr.description: Volkswagen prépare la vente de son usine d'Osnabrück au fonds israélien Aurelius Capital et au Land de Basse-Saxe. Sa reconversion dans la défense pourrait préserver 1 400 emplois sur 1 800, avec Rafael et le Dôme de fer comme premier grand projet.

france24fr.title: Guinée : l'ex magistrat Algassimou Diallo transféré vers la prison de Macenta
france24fr.description: L'ex magistrat Algassimou Diallo, inculpé pour des soupçons de collusion avec un opposant politique en exil, vient d'être transféré vers une prison éloignée de Conakry, la capitale de la Guinée. L'ancien avocat général près de la Cour suprême se trouve désormais à Macenta, ce qui inquiète ses avocats.

france24fr.title: France : les pompiers se mobilisent après un été aux incendies virulents
france24fr.description: Suite aux incendies intenses et violents de cet été, les pompiers se mobilisent pour obtenir plus de moyens financiers, matériels et humains. Chaque année, les équipes couvrent 5 millions d'interventions sur tout le territoire.

france24fr.title: Immigration : naufrage meurtrier, ouverture du procès des 14 passeurs présumés à Paris
france24fr.description: Ouverture du procès de 14 passeurs poursuivis pour leur implication présumée dans la mort ou la disparition de 31 migrants, dont un enfant, au cours de la nuit du 24 novembre 2021 dans la Manche. L'embarcation avait fait naufrage à 15 km de Calais. Le bilan est le plus meurtrier des tentatives de traversée de migrants vers l'Angleterre.

france24fr.title: En grève, les pompiers français en appellent à l'État : "On est traités comme du bétail !"
france24fr.description: En première ligne depuis juin face aux mégafeux subis par plusieurs régions de France, tout en continuant d'assurer au quotidien les secours à la personne – et jusqu'à des missions qui ne leur incombent normalement pas –, les pompiers sont appelés à une grève de plus de six semaines à compter de mardi. Stéphane Lessire, porte-parole Sud SDIS national, était l'invité de France 24.

france24fr.title: Benjamin Netanyahu accusé d'avoir ignoré une alerte sur le massacre du 7-Octobre
france24fr.description: Une enquête de Haaretz révèle que Benjamin Netanyahu a gardé pour lui une alerte émiratie sur une attaque d'ampleur du Hamas quelques jours avant les attaques terroristes du 7 octobre 2023. Son cabinet rejette catégoriquement l'accusation, tandis que ses adversaires lui réclament des comptes. Certains remettent en cause son maintien au pouvoir.

france24fr.title: Élections régionales en Allemagne : un défilé contre l'extrême droite prend place
france24fr.description: Suite à la victoire de l'AfD en Saxe-Anhalt, les Berlinois se sont mobilisés devant la porte de Brandebourg, symbole de la réunification allemande, pour chercher des solutions contre la montée de ce parti pro-Trump et anti-immigration.

france24fr.title: Ukraine - Russie : reprise des négociations, une trêve pour l'hiver ?
france24fr.description: La Russie a repris ses frappes aériennes sur la capitale ukrainienne, bien que le Kremlin ait signalé aux deux émissaires américains être prêt à reprendre les négociations à partir de cet hiver, menant à une "désescalade" du conflit, selon la déclaration du président Zelensky, cité dans le média américain Axios.i

france24fr.title: Ukraine : la Russie frappe de nouveau Kiev après la visite des émissaires américains
france24fr.description: La Russie a repris dans la nuit ses bombardements sur Kiev, faisant au moins deux morts et huit blessés, après une brève pause lors de la visite inédite des deux émissaires américains pour relancer la discussion.

france24fr.title: La tour Eiffel a rouvert mardi après une grève contre la discrimination envers le personnel féminin
france24fr.description: Au lendemain d'une journée de fermeture, le monument parisien accueille de nouveau le public mardi. Les salariés de la tour Eiffel s'étaient mis en grève, pour dénoncer des "consignes" reçues, ayant conduit à évincer les salariées femmes lors de la visite d'un groupe religieux hindou conservateur.

france24fr.title: Yémen : les Houthis revendiquent une vaste attaque contre l'Arabie saoudite
france24fr.description: Les Houthis yéménites ont déclaré mardi avoir lancé des dizaines de drones et de missiles contre des cibles économiques et militaires en Arabie saoudite en guise de riposte aux plus de 120 frappes menées par Riyad contre le Yémen au cours des trois derniers jours.

france24fr.title: Libéré du Togo, le réalisateur français Gaël Mocaër témoigne sur France 24
france24fr.description: Après plus d'un mois de détention à Lomé, le réalisateur français Gaël Mocaër assure que les conditions de détention "étaient tout à fait acceptables". Il revient sur ces 36 jours d'incertitude vécus aux côtés de son collègue Sebastian Perez Pezzani et de leur fixeur.

france24fr.title: Deux tableaux de Renoir volés dans un musée sur la Côte d'Azur
france24fr.description: Deux tableaux ​ont été dérobés ​mardi du musée Renoir de Cagnes-sur-Mer, à proximité de Nice. Le ⁠maire de la ‌ville a indiqué que ​deux voleurs se ‌sont introduits dans le musée peu avant ‌six heures du ​matin, emportant quatre tableaux. Pris en chasse ​par la ​police, les cambrioleurs ont pris la fuite, abandonnant deux des toiles volées.

france24fr.title: Ligue des champions : Lille de retour dans la cour des grands face au Betis Séville
france24fr.description: De retour en Ligue des champions après une saison en Ligue Europa, Lille reçoit le Betis Séville mardi pour son entrée en lice. L'occasion pour les Dogues d'engranger des points précieux à domicile face à un adversaire à leur hauteur, porté également par un bon début de saison.

france24fr.title: Le programme de l'AfD, "un brun flippant"
france24fr.description: À la Une de la presse ce mardi 8 septembre : le jour d'après en Allemagne, où la victoire, dimanche, de l'AfD en Saxe-Anhalt, est un séisme politique ; la mobilisation, en France, des pompiers pour obtenir plus de moyens après une saison estivale marquée par les incendies ; et une nouvelle tendance (odorante) chez les masculinistes.

france24fr.title: 🔴En direct : la Russie reprend ses frappes meurtrières sur Kiev après trois jours de trêve
Avant la Ligue des champions, Kylian Mbappé croit au Ballon d'Or
france24fr.description: Pour la reprise de la Ligue des champions, le Real Madrid reçoit l’Inter Milan. Interrogé en conférence de presse, Kylian Mbappé estime qu’il a toutes ses chances d’être élu Ballon d’Or.

observador.title: Temporada do Teatro Municipal do Porto arranca dias 18 e 19
observador.description: A temporada arranca dias 18 e 19 com Efectos Especiales, o qual conta com a cidade como "cenário". Para este espectáculo vai ser gravado um plano-sequência no Porto.

observador.title: 70 animais recolhidos em condições inadequadas de higiene
observador.description: As autoridades encontraram muitos dos animais enjaulados e com más condições de higiene. Entre os animais resgatados estavam cães, gatos, aves e outros animais de pequeno porte.

observador.title: Netanyahu já sabia do ataque do 7 de Outubro?
observador.description: Jornal Haaretz revela que líder israelita tomou conhecimento da ofensiva do Hamas 10 dias antes mas não avisou os responsáveis pela segurança.

observador.title: Espectadores nos cinemas quase duplicam em agosto
observador.description: O filme mais visto do ano em Portugal foi Homem-Aranha: Um Novo Dia, com quase 669 mil espectadores em agosto. Segue-se a Odisseia com 363 mil espectadores no mesmo mês.

observador.title: Israel diz que Londres estará do "lado errado da história"
observador.description: O Presidente de Israel considerou a aplicação de sanções e boicotes como um "caminho sem saída" e alertou os países que possam querer juntar-se ao Reino Unido.

observador.title: INE. Custos de construção de casas sobem 6,8% em julho
observador.description: Em julho os preços dos materiais aumentaram 6,3%, contra 6,4% em junho, e os custos com mão-de-obra subiram 7,3%, menos 1,1 pontos percentuais do que no mês anterior.

observador.title: Cinema Chinês em Portugal de 18 a 20 de setembro em Lisboa
observador.description: O evento conta com a apresentação do filme "Her Story", um dos filmes asiáticos mais premiados de 2025. As produções abordam várias perspetivas da sociedade e cultura chinesas.

observador.title: Santa Maria da Feira aprovou o Plano Diretor Municipal
observador.description: A segunda revisão do Plano Diretor Municipal visa reforçar em 11% as áreas destinadas a atividades económicos. O plano quer ainda responder ao crescimento demográfico de Santa Maria da Feira.

observador.title: Sindicato admite manter greve após contraproposta do INEM
observador.description: Questionado sobre a existência de condições para suspender a paralisação marcada para os dias 14 e 28 de setembro, Rui Lázaro afirmou que, com o que está em cima da mesa, não há condições para isso.

observador.title: Dois homens e empresa de Espanha terão ajudado imigração
observador.description: Arguidos são acusados de "fazer entrar e explorar" em Elvas trabalhadores estrangeiros, para os introduzir de forma ilegal no mercado de trabalho. Terão lucrado mais de 324 mil euros com as práticas.

observador.title: Financeiros e informáticos entre emigrantes para Reino Unido
observador.description: Analistas, consultores financeiros e profissionais de informática são as atividades mais predominantes no movimento de portugueses, bem como profissões da área da saúde.

observador.title: Zelensky admite dificuldades na interceção de mísseis russos
observador.description: O Presidente ucraniano relevou que vai reunir-se com países e empresas para discutir novas formas de defesa para Ucrânia. Em causa está a diminuição da taxa de interceção de mísseis russos pelo país.

observador.title: Luís Neves: “Nenhuma das decisões visou o enriquecimento"
observador.description: No arranque da audição parlamentar, o Ministro da Administração Interna destaca trabalho na pasta e afirma que está disponível para todo o escrutínio. Ouça aqui as declarações de Luís Neves.

observador.title: Ébola. Nova epidemia na RDCongo causa mais de 3.200 mortos
observador.description: De acordo com o relatório da autoridade de saúde, 819 doentes estão em isolamento ou hospitalizados. O número de casos confirmados aumentou para 6.686. A assistência médica está a ser reforçada.

observador.title: Projeto BIOsCherry quer aumentar qualidade da cereja
observador.description: O projeto BIOsCherry, financiado em 307 mil euros, vai experimentar bioestimulantes em vários tipos de cerejas para aumentar a sua qualidade e produção.

observador.title: Mulheres fumadoras com risco de infertilidade 40% maior
observador.description: A Organização Mundial da Saúde alerta para o aumento da infertilidade como um dos riscos associados ao tabagismo, que pode afetar tanto mulheres como homens.

observador.title: Netanyahu terá ignorado avisos sobre ataque do 7 de outubro
observador.description: Livro baseado em entrevistas diz que Presidente dos Emirados alertou Netanyahu para uma ofensiva do Hamas. Primeiro-ministro terá reagido "com tranquilidade" e não informou segurança. Telavive nega.

observador.title: SOM Saúde Mental: uma visão 360º
observador.description: E se, num só local, pudesse ter acesso a informação simples, fidedigna e esclarecedora sobre saúde mental? O SOM Saúde Mental 360º é a plataforma onde isto se torna possível e chega agora a Portugal.

spiegel.title: Pisa-Studie und die Reaktionen: »Es nützt nichts, zu lamentieren«
spiegel.description: Deutschlands Bildungsminister zeigen sich von den desaströsen Pisa-Ergebnissen wenig überrascht. Der bisherige Kurs wird verteidigt und zur Geduld gemahnt. Ein Ex-Bildungssenator hingegen fordert ein Sofortprogramm.

spiegel.title: Ungarn: Budapest weist zehn russische Diplomaten aus
spiegel.description: Mit der Abwahl Orbáns hat Budapest seinen Kurs gegenüber Moskau geändert. Nun müssen auf Anweisung der Außenministerin zehn Gesandte des Kreml Ungarn verlassen: Ihre Aktivitäten seien nicht mit der Wiener Konvention vereinbar.

spiegel.title: Energiewende: Anteil erneuerbarer Energien an deutscher Stromerzeugung auf Rekordhoch
spiegel.description: Deutschland hat im ersten Halbjahr weniger Strom importiert, mehr exportiert und anteilig mehr grüne Energie erzeugt als je zuvor. Wichtigster Energieträger bleibt dabei die Windkraft.

spiegel.title: DFB-Pokal: Ermittlungen gegen Polizisten nach mutmaßlichem Pyro-Wurf in Mannheim
spiegel.description: Nach den Ausschreitungen im Derby zwischen Mannheim und Kaiserslautern mit mehreren Verletzten gerät ein Polizist in den Fokus der Ermittler. Aufnahmen sollen zeigen, wie er einen brennenden Gegenstand in Richtung der Fans wirft.

spiegel.title: Anschläge auf Umspannwerke: Polizei fasst mutmaßlichen Strom-Saboteur
spiegel.description: Der mutmaßliche Strom-Saboteur ist nach SPIEGEL-Informationen gefasst. Die Polizei nahm den Mann in Nordrhein-Westfalen fest, er hatte offenbar weitere Sprengmittel dabei.

spiegel.title: Erziehung: Warum falsches Lob Kinder eher zum Schummeln verleitet
spiegel.description: »Du bist so schlau«: Viele Eltern preisen ihre Kinder nach Erfolgen, um sie anzuspornen. Die Komplimente können jedoch ungewollt nach hinten losgehen.

spiegel.title: Arbeitsmarkt: Mehr Kinderbetreuung steigert laut Studie den Verdienst von Müttern
spiegel.description: Der Ausbau von Kinderbetreuung führt bei Frauen zu mehr Vollzeitjobs. Forscher sehen auch langfristig einen positiven Effekt auf den Verdienst von Müttern.

spiegel.title: Sachsen-Anhalt: Wer künftig für die AfD im Magdeburger Landtag sitzt
spiegel.description: Neonazi-Gastgeber, Urkundenfälscher, Stasi-Offizier: Unter den 39 künftigen AfD-Abgeordneten im Magdeburger Landtag sind einige Männer mit bedenklichem Hintergrund – darunter zwei Personen, die einem verbotenen Neonazi-Verein nahestehen sollen.

spiegel.title: Fachkräftemangel: Internationale Studierende bringen Milliardenüberschuss für Staat
spiegel.description: Weit mehr internationale Studierende bleiben dauerhaft in Deutschland als bislang geschätzt: Das zeigt ein neues Gutachten des Instituts der deutschen Wirtschaft. Die Entwicklung hat auch Folgen für die Staatskasse.

spiegel.title: Langeweile im Job: Was gegen Stress, Schlafprobleme und Tinnitus hilft
spiegel.description: Ödet Ihr Job Sie an? 60 Prozent der Arbeitnehmer in Deutschland fühlen sich unterfordert, ihnen drohen Folgen für Körper und Psyche. Doch es gibt ein Rezept gegen den Trott: Ein Museumsaufseher hat es gefunden.

spiegel.title: Krieg Russlands gegen die Ukraine: London sagt Kyjiw 100 Millionen Pfund zu – Tote nach Angriffen in der Hauptstadt
spiegel.description: Die Ukraine benötigt dringend Unterstützung bei der Flugabwehr und bekommt sie nun von Großbritannien. Indes sind in Kyjiw zwei Menschen nach russischen Angriffen gestorben.

spiegel.title: Konjunktur: Deutsche Exporte gehen zurück – Auftragsplus in Elektroindustrie
spiegel.description: Wegen sinkender Nachfrage haben deutsche Firmen im Juli weniger Waren exportiert. Doch es gibt auch gute Nachrichten: Eine Branche meldet ein kräftiges Auftragsplus und die Aussicht auf neue Jobs.

spiegel.title: Israel - Gaza: Mohammed bin Zayed (VAE) soll Benjamin Netanyahu vor Hamas-Attacke am 7. Oktober explizit gewarnt haben
spiegel.description: Das Telefonat dauerte wohl 45 Minuten: Mohammed bin Zayed hat Benjamin Netanyahu offenbar im Herbst 2023 vor einer Invasion der Hamas gewarnt. Israels Premier weist den Bericht kategorisch zurück.

spiegel.title: Quiz des Tages beim SPIEGEL: 7 Fragen zum Allgemeinwissen pro Tag
spiegel.description: Jeden Tag gibt es sieben Fragen zu den wichtigsten Themengebieten des politisch-gesellschaftlichen Geschehens. Testen Sie hier Ihr Wissen!

spiegel.title: Bundesversammlung: Schwarz-rot hat bei Bundespräsidentenwahl klare Mehrheit
spiegel.description: Wer beerbt Frank-Walter Steinmeier im Amt des Bundespräsidenten? Das entscheidet die Bundesversammlung im kommenden Januar. Zumindest rechnerisch sind die Verhältnisse nun klar – trotz zwei weiterer Landtagswahlen.

spiegel.title: Bundeswehr: Rudolf Scharping warnt vor Verharmlosung von Bedrohungen
spiegel.description: Als SPD-Verteidigungsminister schickte Rudolf Scharping vor 25 Jahren die Bundeswehr nach Afghanistan. Heute sagt er: »Wir werden zur Wehrpflicht zurückkehren.« Wie blickt er auf seinen Nachfolger Boris Pistorius?

spiegel.title: Deutscher Buchpreis: Dana Vowinckel und Elias Hirschl auf der Shortlist 2026
spiegel.description: Der Deutsche Buchpreis hat seine sechs Kandidaten für die Auszeichnung 2026 bekannt gegeben. Darunter sind eine große Liebesgeschichte von Dana Vowinckel und ein Erzählexperiment von Elias Hirschl.

spiegel.title: Frankreich: Diebe stehlen drei Renoir-Gemälde aus Museum
spiegel.description: Knapp ein Jahr nach dem Überfall auf den Louvre ist Kunsträubern ein weiterer Coup gelungen: In Südfrankreich hatten sie es auf Werke des Impressionisten Pierre-Auguste Renoir abgesehen. Der Schaden geht in die Millionen.

letemps.title: Jusqu’où ira la disgrâce de Jordan Bardella?

phys-org.title: Super-resolution imaging reveals that cohesin prevents local mixing of compact, active genome domains
phys-org.description: The human genome is about two meters (6.6 feet) long, yet it is folded inside a cell nucleus only about 10 micrometers in diameter. To fit into this tiny space, DNA is wrapped around histone proteins to form nucleosomes, which are further organized into chromatin. For decades, chromatin has often been described in two simple forms: euchromatin, which is active, open and accessible, and heterochromatin, which is more compact and repressed.

phys-org.title: Praying for rain as fires, haze plague Indonesian Borneo
phys-org.description: Wildfires ravaging the Indonesian part of Borneo are choking communities as far away as Malaysia with putrid haze, testing the resources and resolve of those who must endure it.

phys-org.title: Worm's radical transformation shows metamorphosis can change the functions of cells
phys-org.description: A squishy worm that starts its life as something of a floating head in the Pacific Ocean is changing what scientists know about metamorphosis at the cellular level.

phys-org.title: AI model decodes cell signaling fingerprints across diverse cell types
phys-org.description: As an embryo develops from a small cluster of stem cells, those once "blank slate" cells begin to take on more specialized roles like brain, liver or muscle cells and organize themselves into three-dimensional structures such as tissues and organs.

phys-org.title: Rearranged polymer chains create degradable materials with potential for stronger, tougher packaging
phys-org.description: What if the key to making stronger, more sustainable plastics isn't changing their ingredients, but rearranging their molecules? Virginia Tech researchers have put that idea to the test, creating degradable polymers with a new molecular architecture that combines properties often difficult to achieve in one material: strength, toughness, flexibility and the ability to block oxygen.

phys-org.title: How beavers can help create fire breaks as part of a drought preparation plan
phys-org.description: Most of the countryside around the Holnicote estate in Somerset has been dry and dusty for most of the summer. But one corner remains conspicuously green.

phys-org.title: Changing the antibiotic playbook to catch an ESKAPE artist
phys-org.description: Nearly a century ago, a single colony of Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) helped launch the antibiotic age. In 1928, Alexander Fleming returned to his London lab to find that a stray mold had wiped out the Staphylococcus growing on one of his plates. The accident gave the world penicillin, ushering in the age of biomedicine and ensuring that an infected cut or scrape would not be fatal.

phys-org.title: Early Earth's auroral belts may have formed a natural ion-beam reactor for prebiotic chemistry
phys-org.description: We usually think of auroras as beautiful lights in the night sky. I see them as visible traces of a connection between the sun, Earth's magnetic field and the atmosphere. This led me to an origin-of-life question: Could the planetary structure that produces auroras also have organized chemical reactions on early Earth?

phys-org.title: Crime is falling—but the public doesn't feel safer, UK study finds
phys-org.description: Crime levels are falling for most offenses across the UK—but the public doesn't necessarily feel safer. It's a human trait to focus on frightening information in the news or on social media—but it could also mean that people are more fearful about crime than they need to be.

phys-org.title: How Indigenous Protected Areas became a vital way to protect nature in Australia
phys-org.description: When you think of conservation in Australia, chances are you'll think of a national park.

phys-org.title: Park rangers and residents speak up to save Togo's last national park
phys-org.description: A few years ago, I drove with an old friend from Togo, West Africa, towards the country's last remaining large protected area, Fazao-Malfakassa National Park. Our destination was the Hotel Fazao, where his uncle had once worked as a professional chef after its opening in 1980. For decades, while the park was managed by the Swiss Franz Weber Foundation (FWF), the hotel had hosted tourists from around the world who came to see elephants, monkeys, and other wildlife for which Africa is famous.

phys-org.title: AI governance model inspired by Pope Leo XIV aims to put ethics first
phys-org.description: Researchers at the John Paul II Catholic University of Lublin (KUL) and the University of Eastern Finland have developed a new model of artificial intelligence governance inspired by the teachings of Pope Leo XIV as set out in his encyclical Magnifica Humanitas. The new model is intended to ensure that AI technologies are developed and used safely, fairly and with full respect for human rights.

phys-org.title: Bumpy battery surfaces can masquerade as nanoscale ion pathways, misleading material design
phys-org.description: A signal that appears to show ions moving inside a battery may, in fact, be an illusion caused by an uneven surface. A KAIST research team has identified the origin of this type of artifact, which can lead researchers to misinterpret what is happening inside a battery, and has developed a method to reduce it.

phys-org.title: War drama Pressure depicts D‑day's weather forecast—what we found when we recreated the challenge using modern systems
phys-org.description: Meteorologist James Stagg gave what many regard as the most important weather forecast in history in June 1944. The fate of more than 150,000 Allied troops preparing to invade the Normandy beaches on D-Day and the future of the war in Europe depended on Stagg and his forecasting teams. Get the forecast wrong and an already perilous invasion might not succeed, prolonging the war. In the briefing room at Southwick House near Portsmouth, waiting for the forecast, sat General Dwight D. Eisenhower.

phys-org.title: Survey of young researchers raises concerns over future of science in U.S.

undark.title: Book Review: The Messy Business of Making Science Happen
undark.description: In “Lost in Curiosity: Field Notes From Scientists’ Adventures Into the Unknown,” Roberta Kwok sets out to smash the stereotype of eureka moments as the main drivers of scientific knowledge, largely by taking us inside the everyday world of science and scientists, in all its painstaking monotony.

undark.title: Book Review: Our Conflicted Relationship with the Sun
undark.description: Despite dermatological guidelines that decree sunlight a harmful carcinogen, Rowan Jacobsen argues in “In Defense of Sunlight” that the sun helps our skin produce many compounds vital to our health. How did science miss these benefits? The answer, he says, lies in our inability to do things in moderation.

undark.title: The New Student Visa Policy Doesn’t Add Up
undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

proj-syn.title: The Digital Wellness Industry Is Hijacking Women’s Health
proj-syn.description: Menopause and perimenopause, long under-researched and dismissed, have become a growth industry for online advertisers and wellness companies. Mining intimate data, this lucrative digital ecosystem exploits medical uncertainty to sell women hormones and supplements they don't need, or that can even harm them.

proj-syn.title: Who Controls the Data Controls the Future
proj-syn.description: While AI is becoming increasingly central to finance, defense, health care, and public administration, it depends on resources most governments do not control: the data used to train it and the compute that processes it. Unless this changes, countries will remain subject to decisions made in boardrooms they cannot influence.

proj-syn.title: Will Europe Be as Unprepared as Ukraine Was?
proj-syn.description: With Russia ramping up its hybrid war, Europe must choose. It can invest in its own defense, accept the trade-offs involved, and build credible deterrence, or it can continue to underspend, hope that diplomacy will suffice, assume that US protection will always be available, and tell itself that the war in Ukraine is a local affair.

proj-syn.title: The Case for a Cashflow Tax
proj-syn.description: In the context of the US economy, a cashflow tax would offer far-reaching benefits in promoting economic growth, taxing rents, and raising incremental revenue efficiently. Moreover, well-known concerns about complexity and fairness are easily addressed.

proj-syn.title: Kevin Warsh’s Best Move Is to Do Nothing
proj-syn.description: Beholden to mainstream economic ideas, the new US Federal Reserve chair has committed himself, and his reputation, to a goal he cannot achieve. Reining in inflation requires not interest-rate adjustments but much larger strategic shifts that are not within the Fed’s power to influence.

proj-syn.title: How Developing Countries Can Do More With Less
proj-syn.description: Evaluation frameworks for development projects have long been influenced by donor priorities. But foreign-aid cuts have created an opportunity for African countries to implement equitable evaluation practices, both to channel limited resources more effectively and to shape the future of global development governance.

proj-syn.title: America’s Naval Disaster
proj-syn.description: Plagued by exorbitant costs and chronic delays, American shipbuilders cannot produce enough vessels to keep pace with China. US President Donald Trump’s push to rebuild the industry does little to address its underlying problems and threatens to squander hundreds of billions of dollars.

proj-syn.title: America’s Un-American AI Companies
proj-syn.description: The United States can prevail in the AI race against China by leaning into the strengths of an open society: democratic oversight, the rule of law, robust competition, and open public debate. But that won’t happen as long as American AI companies aggressively lobby against accountability and cozy up to the state.

proj-syn.title: The Golden Bridge to Monetary Multipolarity
proj-syn.description: Gold has overtaken US Treasuries as the world’s top reserve asset because it offers a solution to the challenges of a rogue America. But its renewed relevance also reflects how rapid technological diffusion and increasing dispersion of economic power are creating a more diversified international monetary system.

proj-syn.title: Asia’s Natural Disasters Must Not Become Financial Crises
proj-syn.description: The dangerous flooding in Nepal and Tibet has demonstrated, once again, the need for prearranged disaster-risk financing to prepare for the economic chain reactions triggered by natural disasters. Asia’s policymakers must act now to help cash-strapped Nepal and strengthen other countries’ resilience before the next crisis hits.

proj-syn.title: Is AI Crowding Out Other Investment?
proj-syn.description: The AI investment boom has unleashed a wave of demand for capital just as savings are declining and interest rates remain high. As competition for financing intensifies, rising borrowing costs could squeeze non-AI firms looking to finance new factories, equipment, and projects.

proj-syn.title: India’s Resilience Depends on Diversified Trade
proj-syn.description: India has signed a flurry of trade deals since Donald Trump’s return to the White House in an attempt to ensure that no single bilateral rupture will cause catastrophic harm. It should continue to expand its trade ties, while being wary of any bilateral agreement that curtails its freedom of action vis-à-vis third countries.

proj-syn.title: Whipsaw Trade Policy Is Depressing Foreign Direct Investment
proj-syn.description: If a country opts for higher trade restrictions to promote its perceived domestic interests, a predictable policy is far superior to a volatile one. As new research shows, uncertainty causes unnecessary and large collateral damage to FDI inflows.

proj-syn.title: Why the Far Right’s War on Modern Architecture Matters
proj-syn.description: The Alternative for Germany’s fixation on architecture is more revealing than it may seem. Cultural policy is not only one area where the party can actually change conditions on the ground at the state level; it is also intimately tied to far-right forces’ exclusionary political agenda.

proj-syn.title: How Will the US-Iran War End?
proj-syn.description: The latest US effort to subdue Iran—an "economic D-Day" intended to cut off the Islamic Republic from the world economy—can’t succeed without the support of the country’s biggest trade partner. The only stable solution to the impasse in the Gulf is one that involves China and increases economic integration in the region.

proj-syn.title: Germany’s Political Firewall Is Crumbling
proj-syn.description: The upcoming election in Saxony-Anhalt could give the far-right Alternative für Deutschland control of a state government for the first time in Germany’s postwar history. Its rise offers a crucial lesson for democracies elsewhere: closing ranks against extremist parties is no substitute for effective governance.

proj-syn.title: The Swimmable City Test
proj-syn.description: In committing to provide a safe swimmable place within 15 minutes of every home by 2035, London Mayor Sadiq Khan has set a measurable, time-bound goal that cannot be met through a single program or line item on the budget. Instead, it requires a public mission capable of mobilizing all ministries and shaping markets.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: Crusoe And Fluidstack Lead Multibillion-Dollar AI Infrastructure Haul
crunchbase.description: AI infrastructure dominated the largest venture rounds this week, with two multibillion-dollar deals in the sector taking the top spots. Data center and cloud provider Crusoe led with a massive $3 billion financing, followed by Fluidstack’s $1.5 billion raise.

crunchbase.title: A Startup General Counsel Knew What Corporate Lawyers Needed From AI. So She Built It.
crunchbase.description: After nearly two decades working as a lawyer at companies such as Amazon, Cruise, Replit and Anki, Cecilia Ziniti teamed up with engineer Bardia Pourvakil to combine their knowledge of law and coding to co-found GC AI.

crunchbase.title: Global Venture Funding Jumps 122% In August As Streak Of Billion-Dollar Deals Continues
crunchbase.description: Venture investors poured $42 billion into just over 1,500 startups worldwide in August, Crunchbase data shows, down 25% from July’s $56 billion but still up a significant 122% compared to last August, which is typically a slower month for startup investment.

crunchbase.title: Former Apple Engineers’ Physical AI Startup Lyte Raises $165M At $1.6B Valuation
crunchbase.description: Lyte, a physical AI startup building sensing and perception technology for robots, has raised a Maverick Silicon-led $165 million Series C funding at a $1.6 billion post-money valuation.

crunchbase.title: The IPO Window Is Closing. Here Are 8 Startups To Watch.
crunchbase.description: In the first half of this year, 58 venture-backed companies joined the public listings at $1 billion or above, per Crunchbase data. With the year’s end now in sight, a small window remains for other startups to launch 2026 IPOs, so we took a look at notable venture-backed startups that Crunchbase’s predictive intelligence suggests are potential IPO candidates within the next six months.

crunchbase.title: WhatsApp Remittance Startup Félix Secures $200M Series C Led By A16z, General Catalyst
crunchbase.description: Félix, a Miami-based AI-powered WhatsApp remittance platform for Latino immigrants, announced on Tuesday that it has secured $200 million in Series C funding co-led by Andreessen Horowitz and General Catalyst.

crunchbase.title: Sector Snapshot: Proptech Funding Holds Up, But Investors Are Placing Different Bets
crunchbase.description: Real estate tech startup investors are being more selective about their bets and putting more money into companies using AI and other technology to make construction, property operations and real estate transactions faster and less expensive.

crunchbase.title: Biotech Startup Investment Held Steady Even As AI Funding Surged
crunchbase.description: While the AI boom has disrupted funding patterns across the startup sphere, biotech has remained a rare steady sector for investment. For the past few years, global funding to biotech startups has hovered between $36 billion and $40 billion. Per Crunchbase data, 2026 is on track to stay close to that range.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: AI Tools And Assistants Lead Sparser Lineup Of Megadeals
crunchbase.description: Most of this week’s largest funding recipients were AI-focused startups, with Instinct, a developer of AI assistants, pulling in the biggest round.

crunchbase.title: Sector Snapshot: Space Tech Startup Funding Orbits New Highs
crunchbase.description: So far this year, a record $20.3 billion in global seed- through growth-stage funding has gone to companies in space- and satellite-related sectors, per Crunchbase data. That’s already by far the highest annual tally on record, and we’ve still got four months left in 2026.
